extracted.intended_audience: covered entities (health care providers, health insurers, pharmacies), health program administrators, legal counsel, and stakeholders affected by HHS Section 1557 nondiscrimination rules
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and implementation guidance for Section 1557 of the ACA prohibiting discrimination in covered health programs or activities, with specific provisions on sex discrimination related to marital/parental/family status, pregnancy-related conditions, insurance coverage, pharmacies, and conscience protections. Includes examples, scope, and interactions with title IX, HIPAA, EMTALA, and other federal statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using sex when applying marital/parental/family status rules (§92.208)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 92.208 prohibits a covered entity from implementing a policy related to marital, parental, or family status that treats individuals differently on the basis of sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: impermissible distinctions include allowing male spouses of women to make medical decisions for their children but not non-male spouses of women, or allowing visitation for a married heterosexual couple but denying visitation for a married same-sex couple. The rule targets differences in application based on sex, not distinctions tied solely to marital status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted distinctions based on marital status alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities may make distinctions based upon marital status alone (e.g., applying different rules to married and nonmarried individuals) so long as those distinctions do not distinguish based on an individual's sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies §92.208 is not a prohibition against policies that differentiate married from unmarried persons per se; it prohibits differential treatment that is driven by sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscriminatory insurance/benefit coverage for fertility treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered health insurance issuer that offers fertility coverage or treatments for married different-sex couples may not deny the same coverage or treatments to married same-sex couples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted institutional definitions of 'infertility' can create discriminatory barriers for same-sex couples; OCR states that issuers who offer benefits must offer them in a nondiscriminatory manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies tied to marital/parental/family status are unlawful only when applied differently by sex
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and procedures that include conditions or limitations tied to marital, parental, or family statuses do not violate §92.208 unless they apply differently based on the sex of the individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR warns against conflating prohibition on sex discrimination with a prohibition on marital/familial status per se; enforcement focuses on sex-based disparate application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on denial of care on basis of association (§92.209 cross-reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusing to see a prospective patient because of the sex of the patient's spouse (for example, refusing to see a female patient because she has a female spouse) constitutes sex discrimination related to marital status and may also constitute discrimination on the basis of association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR explicitly agrees a medical practice may not refuse a female patient solely because she has a female spouse if the practice otherwise accepts married individuals; such refusals are treated as sex discrimination and related to association (§92.209).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy and related conditions are forms of sex discrimination (§92.101(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination on the basis of sex includes 'pregnancy or related conditions'; covered entities may not discriminate against individuals for pregnancy-related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR understands the term to include childbirth, false pregnancy, termination of pregnancy, ectopic pregnancy, miscarriage, and recovery therefrom, but does not intend the regulatory language to be exhaustive. OCR placed 'pregnancy or related conditions' in §92.101(a)(2) rather than §92.208 to avoid implying limitation to marital/parental contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for pregnancy-related decisions (past, present, future)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1557, covered entities may not discriminate against individuals for their pregnancy-related decisions, past, present, or future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protection applies broadly; OCR will consider such claims and looks to relevant statutes and case law when evaluating whether discrimination occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACA conscience and abortion-related statutory limits on rule application
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the ACA or this rule affects federal laws regarding conscience protection, willingness or refusal to provide abortion, or discrimination based on willingness to provide, pay for, cover, or refer for abortion; providers may decline to provide abortions for conscience, religious, or nondiscriminatory business reasons without necessarily violating section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited statutory authority: 42 U.S.C. 18023(c)(1)-(2). OCR emphasizes the rule does not create a federal right to abortion, does not preempt State abortion laws, and recognizes other federal protections (e.g., Weldon, Coats-Snowe, Church Amendments). OCR will evaluate conflicts and exemptions (including religious/conscience claims) on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR will evaluate pregnancy-related discrimination using title IX and section 1557 case law
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will consider complaints of sex discrimination, including discrimination based on pregnancy or related conditions, on a case-by-case basis and will look to title IX and section 1557 case law to determine whether discrimination has occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR notes its longstanding interpretation of sex discrimination is consistent with title IX's inclusion of pregnancy-related discrimination since 1975; however, OCR will not treat a provider's decision not to provide abortions per se as a §1557 violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections and HIPAA considerations for pregnancy-related information
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities may not discriminate against individuals for pregnancy-related decisions including where the patient discloses the information or where such information is contained in medical records; HIPAA protects sensitive patient health information from disclosure without consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR is separately considering revisions to the HIPAA Privacy Rule to strengthen privacy protections for reproductive health information (see HIPAA Privacy Rule NPRM referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to lawful prescription medications and pharmacy obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a covered entity denies or delays lawful access to medications (including medications prescribed for conditions unrelated to abortion), that refusal could violate section 1557 if the refusal is on the basis of a prohibited ground such as race, age, disability, or sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: refusing an antibiotic for a miscarriage-related infection because of concern about potential subsequent abortion may be sex discrimination. OCR issued revised guidance to pharmacies; OCR does not require pharmacies to fill prescriptions for abortion or to violate State laws, and will evaluate religious freedom and conscience protections case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 1557 applies across all covered health programs and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557's prohibitions of discrimination apply across all covered health programs and activities administered or funded by HHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR underscores that obligations extend broadly to covered entities and activities, including health insurance issuers that offer benefits and health care providers, subject to statutory limitations and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: EMTALA obligations and emergency care for pregnancy-related conditions unaffected
rubrics_metrics.description: EMTALA protects emergency care for pregnancy-related conditions including termination of pregnancy, and nothing in this rule changes or affects EMTALA obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR does not enforce EMTALA and directs readers to the discussion of EMTALA under §92.3 for related obligations and clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision not to import title IX abortion neutrality provision
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to incorporate title IX's abortion neutrality provision into section 1557 regulations, concluding it is not required and is unnecessary given the ACA's treatment of abortion-related statutory protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR's rationale: the ACA already contains explicit provisions (42 U.S.C. 18023) regarding conscience and abortion coverage that differ from title IX's neutrality provision; importing that language could undermine OCR's implementation of §1557 to eliminate barriers and expand access to health care. OCR reiterates that refusing to provide abortions for certain reasons is not itself a §1557 violation.
